doc.title: Jon-Erik Kellso interviewed by Monk Rowe, Chautauqua, New York, September 12, 1997

title: Henry Ford Community College jazz program and Wayne State
summary: He studied with Jack Pearson at Henry Ford Community College, then Wayne State with Matt Michaels, touring Europe with the band.

venues.name: Henry Ford Community College Jazz Program

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: School days: grades, teachers and leaving school

blocks.x: What about college experience? Did you continue your love of jazz through college?

Yeah. Well like I said, when I was in high school I was playing and getting some summer credits in this program called the Henry Ford Community College Jazz Program, which was directed by a guy names Jack Pearson who was a great teacher and a good influence. And we used to play at the Montreux-Detroit Jazz Festival every summer with that group. And I got to meet a lot of great players there and had some good teachers. And so that’s sort of my beginning of my college jazz training there. And then I went into Wayne State University in Detroit after I graduated from Allen Park High School. I started off being a Jazz Studies major. Matt Michaels was a great piano player teacher there who was directing the band. That was a good experience too. I got to go Europe with that band, and met a lot more good players. And I went to school on and off for about six years at Wayne State. I played in the band and again played at the Montreux Jazz Festival and did other types of concerts with that group. It was good, I enjoyed that.
